To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Tungsten oxide thin films prepared using a peroxo-tungalsten precursor have been found to exhibit photoactivity under visible light.

the photoelectrolytic water splitting activity of tungsten oxide films prepared using a peroxo tungsten precursor is significantly higher than the photoelectrochemical activity of TiO2 films prepared under similar conditions.
the photoelectrochemical performance of tungsten oxide films prepared from peroxo-precursors is superior to that of titanium dioxide films prepared by the same route.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of photoelectrochemical cells using tungsten oxide thin-film photoanodes for the photo-oxidation of water.
the preparation of tungsten oxide thin film photoanodes for the photoelectrolytic oxidation of water under visible light irradiation.
the preparation of tungsten oxide thin film photoanodes for photoelectrochemical water oxidation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tungsten oxide is an excellent material for the photoelectrochemical splitting of water under visible light.
the photoelectrolytic water splitting performance of tungsten oxide thin film electrodes is superior to that of titanium oxide.
WO3 is a good candidate for the photoelectrolytic production of hydrogen under visible light.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photocurrent response from tungsten oxide is more favourable than titanium dioxide, and that this is due to the favourable absorption properties of tungsten oxide.
tungsten oxide thin-films have a potential to replace titanium oxide in the field of photo-electrochemical water splitting.
the photoelectrolytic activity of WO3 is comparable to that of TiO2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the photoelectrode performance can be tuned by controlling the precursor chemistry.
WO3 films can be made to respond to visible light and can be made to be stable in the photoelectrolytic environment.
the electrolytic route for preparing tungsten oxide thin film is a viable route for the development of photoelectrodes for solar water splitting.
